Propose a minimal placeholder workflow structure that could be used once the missing details are provided.Here's a minimal placeholder structure. Design principle: encode only what's structural (start → task → decision → outcomes) and mark every unknown as an explicit `{{PLACEHOLDER}}` so nothing invented silently becomes fact.

## Proposed file: `workflows/PLACEHOLDER-process-draft.bpmn`

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!-- DRAFT PLACEHOLDER — NOT A REAL PROCESS DEFINITION.
     Every {{...}} token must be replaced with user-provided details
     before this file is considered meaningful. -->
<bpmn:definitions xmlns:bpmn="http://www.omg.org/spec/BPMN/20100524/MODEL"
                  id="Definitions_PLACEHOLDER"
                  targetNamespace="http://example.com/placeholder"
                  exporter="draft-placeholder">
  <bpmn:process id="Process_PLACEHOLDER"
                name="{{PROCESS_NAME}}"
                isExecutable="false">

    <!-- Start: trigger unknown -->
    <bpmn:startEvent id="Start_1" name="{{START_TRIGGER}}">
      <bpmn:outgoing>Flow_s_t1</bpmn:outgoing>
    </bpmn:startEvent>

    <!-- Single representative step; real step list unknown -->
    <bpmn:task id="Task_1" name="{{STEP_1_NAME}}">
      <bpmn:incoming>Flow_s_t1</bpmn:incoming>
      <bpmn:outgoing>Flow_t1_g1</bpmn:outgoing>
    </bpmn:task>

    <!-- Decision: condition unknown -->
    <bpmn:exclusiveGateway id="Gateway_1" name="{{DECISION_1_QUESTION}}">
      <bpmn:incoming>Flow_t1_g1</bpmn:incoming>
      <bpmn:outgoing>Flow_g1_end1</bpmn:outgoing>
      <bpmn:outgoing>Flow_g1_end2</bpmn:outgoing>
    </bpmn:exclusiveGateway>

    <bpmn:endEvent id="End_Success" name="{{END_STATE_SUCCESS}}"/>
    <bpmn:endEvent id="End_Failure" name="{{END_STATE_FAILURE}}"/>

    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_s_t1"  sourceRef="Start_1"   targetRef="Task_1"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_t1_g1" sourceRef="Task_1"    targetRef="Gateway_1"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_g1_end1" sourceRef="Gateway_1" targetRef="End_Success"
                        name="{{CONDITION_PASS}}"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_g1_end2" sourceRef="Gateway_1" targetRef="End_Failure"
                        name="{{CONDITION_FAIL}}"/>
  </bpmn:process>
</bpmn:definitions>
```

## Placeholder → missing-detail mapping

| Placeholder | Requires (from the missing-info list) |
|---|---|
| `{{PROCESS_NAME}}` | #1 Process identity |
| `{{START_TRIGGER}}` | #6 Events (min: message/manual) |
| `{{STEP_1_NAME}}` + more steps | #3 Process steps (this skeleton scales to N tasks) |
| `{{DECISION_1_QUESTION}}`, `{{CONDITION_PASS/FAIL}}` | #4 Decision points |
| `isExecutable="false"` | #2 Format/engine — stays `false` until engine is confirmed |

## Notes

- **Intentionally omitted:** lanes (#5), exception/compensation paths (#7), data objects (#8), integrations (#9) — adding them before the real steps are known would compound the guesswork. The structure extends cleanly once details arrive.
- **If the engine turns out non-BPMN** (e.g., Argo/Airflow), the same slots translate directly to a YAML skeleton: `entrypoint: {{START_TRIGGER}}`, one `steps:` entry per `{{STEP_N_NAME}}`, a `when:` conditional per gateway branch. The placeholders are format-agnostic.
- `isExecutable="false"` and the header comment keep the file inert and clearly marked as a draft.

If you want, I can commit this skeleton to the workspace as a clearly-marked draft file next (with the placeholders intact), and run an XML well-formedness check on it.
